newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan claims some Azeri Caspian oil fields.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan claims some Azeri Caspian oil fields.

text.p: Turkmenistan said on Thursday that Azerbaijan's Azeri oil field and part of the Chirag field, both in the Caspian Sea and under development by an $8 billion multinational group, belong to Turkmenistan, not Azerbaijan.

"The Azeri oil field and part of the Chirag field are located in the Turkmen part of the Caspian Sea and therefore fall under Turkmenistan's jurisdiction," the foreign ministry's press spokesman told Reuters.

The latest spat may be a worry to the 13 major international oil companies that form the Azerbaijan International Operating Co (AIOC), which is developing the Azeri, Chirag and deepwater Guneshli offshore oil fields with Azerbaijan.
Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan lie opposite one another on the Caspian Sea, which is the subject of legal and diplomatic quarrels over who owns the body of water's huge reserves of oil and gas.

The five littoral states vying for the Caspian's resources -- Russia, Iran, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan -- failed to meet in December 1996 for scheduled talks to decide its status, which has been in limbo since the collapse of the Soviet Union.
The focus of the squabble is whether the Caspian is a sea or a lake. Some argue the sea is a salt-water lake.
The AIOC venture aims to begin production later this year and produce more than 700,000 barrels per day by 2010.
